summary.headline: Schaeffler India Q3 CY26 revenue rose 27.4% YoY to INR 3,005 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 18.7% and free cash flow fell to INR 41 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 12.1% QoQ and 27.4% YoY to INR 3,005 crore, with Automotive Technologies up 35% YoY and exports up 46.3% YoY. EBITDA was INR 562 crore (18.7% margin, down from 19.1% QoQ) as raw material and energy cost inflation, linked to fuel prices and the West Asia crisis, was only partly recovered from customers. Profit after tax was INR 370 crore (12.3% margin versus 12.6% QoQ). Working capital rose to about 19% of sales on planned localisation stock and unplanned e-mobility inventory, pulling Q3 free cash flow down to INR 41 crore despite INR 182 crore of capex.

financial_highlights.value: INR 182 crore in Q3; INR 357 crore for 9M
financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly capex of the year in Q3

financial_highlights.value: INR 41 crore in Q3; INR 274 crore for 9M

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue incl. KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions

financial_highlights.value: Gross margin improvement of about INR 192 crore; employee cost increase about INR 44 crore; other income impact about INR 62 crore

segments.name: Automotive Technologies
segments.commentary: About 37% of revenue; grew 17.3% QoQ and 35% YoY. Business wins in engine components (lash adjusters, HLA-RFF, roller tappets, rocker arms) and passenger vehicle clutches.

segments.name: Bearings and Industrial Solutions (B&IS)
segments.commentary: About 35% of revenue; grew 10.2% QoQ and 14.7% YoY, and about 8% YTD. Growth drivers were two-wheelers, raw materials, wind and distribution; needle roller bearings grew close to 20%. Wind calibration on price is ongoing. Industrial automation is about 3% of India business.

segments.name: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (aftermarket)
segments.commentary: About 11% of revenue; grew 2% QoQ and 22% YoY. Management expects double-digit growth for the full year on a YTD basis.

segments.name: Exports (intercompany)
segments.commentary: About 17% of revenue, up from 15% last quarter; grew 12.7% QoQ and 46.3% YoY. Europe is about 45% of exports, Asia Pacific 35%, with the rest China and America. Mainly bearings sold to group companies.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions (segment EBIT)
segments.commentary: Segment EBIT margin fell from 13.1% to 12.2%, attributed to adverse sales mix from e-mobility development costs and lower price recovery than B&IS. B&IS segment EBIT margin rose from 21.1% to 22.3%.

guidance_outlook: Input cost recovery: about 1.1% of quarterly sales was hit; about 50% recovered so far and about 50% under negotiation. Management expects 80-85% of past price increases to be recovered, with a lag of 4-6 months, mostly retrospective.
Q4 export run-rate expected to be slightly lower than Q3 (Q3 above INR 500 crore) because orders are frozen for 90 days; not treated as a new baseline.
Working capital and free cash flow recovery targeted in Q4; the e-mobility inventory build is expected to correct by December.
Capex for CY26 of about INR 500 crore will be realised; the CY27 average is close to this and may be slightly higher, with budgets still under preparation.
Localisation target raised from 80% to 85%; traded goods are around 19-20% of revenue.
Automotive demand expected to stay strong into at least some quarters of 2027 per customer discussions; BS7 transition likely around 2029 could drive engine and transmission portfolio revamps.
capex_capacity: Q3 CY26 capex INR 182 crore, the highest quarterly spend this year; 9M capex INR 357 crore.
CY26 capex guidance of about INR 500 crore; the company said it will be realised, but the breakdown across e-axle, Shoolagiri Phase 2, Savli wind bearings and railway was not shared.
Construction of new halls at Savli and Shoolagiri will continue into next year.
Plants are at full capacity utilisation; inventory was built to support operations amid West Asia logistics issues.
Actuators (rotary and linear) are still imported; bearings for industrial automation are made locally. Management is evaluating local production of actuators.
demand_pricing: Automotive demand is strong: India IIP hit a 7.7% high; passenger vehicle production up about 18% YTD, commercial vehicles up about 21% YTD, tractors up about 18% YTD, with GST 2.0 cited as a driver.
Export order book is 90-120 days of intercompany visibility; management cannot give a long-term view. Q3 export spike is partly seasonal, linked to year-end group billing in December.
Europe-related consolidation was not seen in group signals. Management says India is about 25% cheaper than Europe on production cost, and the group also uses Vietnam, Indonesia and Mexico.
Price recovery on input costs is still in negotiation with several customers. Wind customers were calibrated for price increases, and the company will exit business that does not create value.
Railways are tender-driven and lumpy quarter to quarter. Wind exports are a deemed export for the company.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the cumulative input cost inflation has been recovered, and what is the Q4 recovery plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin impact is about 1.1% of quarterly sales; about 50% has been recovered and 50% is under negotiation. Historically 80-85% has been recovered, and management is confident of the same this time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the inventory build due to customer schedule cuts or programme delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Neither. It is due to unbudgeted e-mobility demand that arose in Q3 and Q4, and the build is for Q4 sales. Management expects a correction by December. Logistics issues linked to West Asia also required stock buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Are exports sustainable, and is Q3 a new baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Export orders are on a 90-day frozen window and Q4 is expected to be slightly lower than Q3's run-rate of above INR 500 crore unless a surprise comes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of the Bearings and Industrial Solutions growth, and how much is industrial automation?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from two-wheelers, raw materials, wind and distribution. YTD B&IS growth is about 8%. Industrial automation is about 3% of India business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin mix gap between Mobility and B&IS explained by pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mobility has recovered price increases to a greater extent. Adverse sales mix from e-mobility development costs also weighed on Mobility margins, and new products are priced higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex be higher in CY27, and how is the parent stake sale relevant?
qa_highlights.answer: CY26 capex is about INR 500 crore and the CY27 average is similar, possibly slightly higher. The parent intends to reduce its stake to about 67-68%. Management says it is a minor monetisation, with no exact figures yet, and that no Vitesco India merger is planned.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery: about 50% of the INR 1.1% of sales hit is still under negotiation; the 4-6 month lag means Q4 may not fully recover.
Free cash flow: INR 41 crore in Q3 and 9M FCF of INR 274 crore; working capital is about 19% of sales and debtor collections are still being worked on.
Export durability: Q3 spike partly seasonal and orders are on a 90-day window; Q4 is guided slightly lower.
Parent stake sale: the promoter intends to reduce holding from about 75% toward 67-68%; timing and size are unknown.
Commercial vehicle cycle and tractor monsoon risk; management expects automotive strength through some quarters of 2027.
Adverse mix from e-mobility development costs is weighing on Mobility segment margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the order pipeline, but cautious and somewhat defensive on margins, working capital and free cash flow, which management repeatedly said are still work in progress. Evasive on long-term export visibility, parent stake-sale details, and capex breakdown, and it declined to give some specifics.
key_quotes: The good news is our capex framework still remains strong.
So, it is not that they will put all the eggs in one basket.
We will be realizing these INR 500 crores surely, but the breakup cannot be shared.
Historically, we have been able to recover approximately 80% to 85% of such price increases, and we are very confident that the sales teams will succeed this time as well.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin slipped to 18.7% from 19.1% QoQ; about 50% of the 1.1% of sales input-cost hit is recovered and 50% still under negotiation, with 80-85% recovery expected on a 4-6 month lag, so recovery is conditional.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plants at full utilisation, with Shoolagiri Phase 2 and Savli wind bearings halls under construction (completion around Q4 per brief) and CY26 capex of about INR 500 crore; breakdown not shared, so timing is only partly specified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 27.4% YoY to INR 3,005 crore and Automotive Technologies rose 35% YoY; PV production up about 18% YTD and CV up about 21% YTD, though Q4 exports are guided slightly below Q3's above INR 500 crore run-rate.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Plants are at full utilisation and CY27 capex is guided at about INR 500 crore or slightly higher, but budgets are still being prepared and no new project has a date; actuators local production is only being evaluated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was given; management called margins, working capital and FCF work in progress, and Q4 exports are guided slightly lower than Q3.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 exports are guided slightly below Q3, the e-mobility inventory correction is expected by December, and FCF was only INR 41 crore in Q3 with 9M FCF of INR 274 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Business wins in engine components (lash adjusters, HLA-RFF, roller tappets, rocker arms) and PV clutches are noted, and BS7 around 2029 could drive engine portfolio revamps, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Working capital and FCF recovery in Q4
rows.why: Working capital is about 19% of sales and Q3 FCF fell to INR 41 crore; management targets recovery in Q4 as the e-mobility inventory build corrects by December.

rows.label: Input cost price recovery
rows.why: About 50% of the 1.1% of quarterly sales hit is recovered, with 50% under negotiation and 80-85% recovery expected on a 4-6 month lag, mostly retrospective.

rows.label: Parent stake sale to 67-68%
rows.why: Promoter intends to cut holding from about 75% toward 67-68%, but management calls it a minor monetisation with no figures or timing given.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line growth, demand and the order pipeline, but cautious and somewhat defensive on margins, working capital and FCF; analysts probed input-cost recovery, the inventory build, export sustainability and the parent stake sale.
